meta.title: Gradient descent in 45 seconds
meta.audience: Curious newcomers to machine learning; no calculus assumed
meta.goal: Viewer can say, in one sentence, how a model improves: measure the error, find the downhill direction, take a small step, repeat.

scenes.purpose: Pose the question the video answers.
scenes.narration: How does a model actually learn? One rule, repeated billions of times.

visual.notes: Kicker label fades in, question rises word by word; 'learn' gets the accent colour.

scenes.purpose: Stakes: modern models have enormous numbers of parameters, all tuned by the same rule.
on_screen_text: each nudged by one simple rule

visual.notes: Counter climbs to 175 billion; caption underneath.

scenes.purpose: Show the update rule and name each term.

visual.notes: KaTeX equation centred; hand-drawn circles around η and ∇L with labels.

scenes.purpose: The loss is a landscape; each step walks downhill.

visual.notes: Filled contours of the loss; a dot follows the precomputed descent path, the path draws behind it.

scenes.purpose: Same landscape in 3D, so 'downhill' is literal.

visual.notes: Three.js surface of the same loss, slow orbit, ball rolling down the path.

scenes.purpose: Step size matters: too small is slow, too large diverges.

visual.notes: Three loss curves drawn in sequence; 'too large' dashed in warning colour.

scenes.purpose: Refinements of the same idea converge faster.

visual.notes: Horizontal bars, Adam highlighted. Illustrative numbers, labelled as such.

scenes.purpose: The whole training loop in one picture.

visual.notes: Five boxes left-to-right, arrows draw in reading order, a curved arrow loops back from Update to Model.
